reason: The geometry is real but the reading of it is wrong, the proposed fix breaks a passing gate, and it is measurably worse on the phone. MEASURED (disclosure forced open, owner-flight/phone/desk, the only three states with behind rows): at 390 the two dated titles sit at x=132 and the cancelled title at x=20; at 1440 they sit at x=698/699 and x=586/587. That much of the finding checks out. Everything built on top of it does not. (1) It restates a gate assertion, inverted. interaction-check.mjs line ~1666 carries a named, passing check written for exactly this rule -- ok('an empty lane reserves nothing', lane === 'none') at 390/record/desk, sitting under the comment 'A cancelled row has no date, and the empty lane went on reserving 96px while the machine's label took more room than the couple's own words.' I ran that assertion as shipped (lane='none', passes) and with the proposed fix injected (lane='block'). Deleting b.css:474 fails the behaviour gate. The lane collapse is not an oversight; it is a paid-for fix from a prior round with a regression test guarding it. (2) The fix is worse where it matters most. At 390 with .b-behindDate:empty restored and .b-behindState set to flex:0 1 auto/min-width:0, the row does not tidy up: 96+16+121.2+16+105.6 = 354.8 exceeds the 350px row, so 'Not going ahead' drops to a second flex line and, still carrying margin-left:auto, hangs right-aligned and orphaned under an empty 96px gutter. Row height goes 38.5 to 65.9. The audience the brief names opens this once, on a phone; the fix trades a clean one-line record for a two-line one with a hole in it and a floating machine label. Only 768 and above get the tidier column, and even there it is bought with a visible empty gutter. (3) The 'by the file's own standard' argument misreads the print comment. I ran the counterfactual: restore flex and the 96px lane on the .b-print row and the three titles land at 492, 380, 380 -- three edges, caused by 220px of paper forcing 'We said yes' to wrap the lane, not by a collapsed lane. The screen row is 350-668px wide and nothing wraps, so the print restack answers a different failure. The as-shipped print sheet already puts all three titles on one edge (x=380 at 1440, x=21 at 390) with the date stacked above; there is nothing to carry over. (4) The alignment charge itself does not hold. The cancelled title is not on a third orphan edge -- it is flush with the block's own left margin, the same edge as the 'BEHIND YOU' heading, the date column, and the closing sentence 'One of them did not happen.' below it. It is a hanging outdent that says this row is not part of the dated sequence, reinforced by the strikethrough and the words, and it is the last row of the block, so nothing sits under it to be knocked out of line. render-b.js:344-352 blanks the date deliberately -- 'A thing that was called off did not fail to have a date' -- so the empty lane is the signal, not the residue of one. (5) Minor but telling: it is a three-row block in every state that has one, not the 'four-row block' the finding describes.
